forces.title: Digital Public Infrastructure as Foundation for Payments Evolution
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), including Aadhaar, UPI, Account Aggregator, and DigiLocker, provides a robust and interoperable foundation for digital financial services. This infrastructure facilitates scaled digital participation and financial inclusion, positioning UPI at the forefront of innovation. For payment systems, DPI enables secure identity verification, real-time transfers, and consent-based data sharing, supporting AI-driven decision-making, and strengthening the ecosystem's ability to evolve towards more intelligent and interconnected financial services at population scale.

forces.title: AI Integration Reshaping Payment System Operations and Intelligence
forces.description: Artificial intelligence is transitioning from a supporting technology to a foundational intelligence layer within financial systems, directly impacting payment infrastructure. AI-native operating models enable real-time decision-making, hyper-personalized experiences, and autonomous workflows across payments. This includes AI-enabled underwriting leveraging UPI behavior, real-time fraud detection through federated intelligence, and automated reconciliation processes. This shift promises significant enhancements in efficiency, risk management, and overall operational resilience for payment mechanisms, moving towards more proactive and context-aware financial operations.

forces.title: Programmable Money and Digital Assets as Payment Infrastructure
forces.description: The emergence of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and stablecoins is profoundly reshaping payment infrastructure by introducing programmable money and tokenized assets. These digital innovations enable conditional, self-executing payment flows through smart contracts, near real-time settlement, and enhanced interoperability across financial markets. Financial institutions are actively exploring stablecoin-enabled networks to modernize cross-border payments, treasury operations, and settlement processes, driving the need for new digital asset infrastructure. This represents a fundamental shift in how value is transferred and managed within the financial ecosystem.

forces.title: RBI's Unified Directives for Digital Payment Security
forces.description: The Reserve Bank of India's consolidated Master Directions, issued on July 31, 2026, for Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, Resilience and Assurance, and Digital Payment Security Controls, represent a significant regulatory structural change. These directives establish a comprehensive framework for payment banks and other regulated entities, covering governance, authentication, application security, and fraud prevention controls. Key mandates include board-approved digital payment policies, six-hour cyber incident reporting, and enhanced vulnerability assessments. This regulatory push aims to strengthen the security and resilience of digital payment ecosystems, directly impacting the operational design and compliance of payment infrastructure.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Inefficiencies in B2B Payment and Information Flows
forces.description: Fragmented information flows and disconnected business systems create significant inefficiencies in B2B payment processes, particularly for MSMEs. Manual processing of invoices, lack of real-time visibility on payment status, and unlinked transaction records lead to extended payment cycles (often 73+ days), high error rates (10-15%), and substantial finance team bandwidth consumption (30-40%). This constrains MSME access to formal working capital and underscores the urgent need for a unified, interoperable digital layer or 'transaction spine' to link payments to invoices, streamline reconciliation, and improve overall B2B payment infrastructure.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Escalating AI-Driven Cybersecurity and Fraud Threats
forces.description: The rapid advancement of AI technologies, particularly Generative AI, introduces significant and evolving cybersecurity and fraud risks to digital payment systems. Attackers can leverage AI to create convincing phishing campaigns, automate vulnerability hunts, deploy deepfakes, and generate synthetic identities that bypass traditional verification controls like video KYC and facial authentication. This expands the attack surface faster than current control environments can adapt, necessitating continuous, real-time intelligence sharing, federated fraud detection across payment rails, and robust governance frameworks to safeguard financial infrastructure and maintain trust.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: Quantum Readiness Becoming Critical for Payment Security
forces.description: The advent of quantum computing poses a long-term, existential threat to the cryptographic security underpinning current digital identities, payments, and financial infrastructure. Consequently, quantum readiness is emerging as a critical strategic priority, driving financial institutions, exchanges, and payment networks to adopt quantum-resistant authentication frameworks and encryption. This necessitates re-examining and upgrading systems once considered immutable to safeguard customer identities and interbank communications. Preparing for future cryptographic risks and technological disruption will be a core component of operational resilience frameworks, ensuring the long-term integrity of payment systems.

forces.title: Significant Global Investment in Payments and Infrastructure
forces.description: The payments sector is attracting substantial global investment, driven by investor confidence in scaled, profitable, and infrastructure-focused businesses. In H1 2026, payments garnered the largest share of fintech investment, with significant capital flowing into both traditional payments infrastructure and emerging areas like digital assets and stablecoins. This investment is bolstered by strategic M&A activities and regulatory developments like MiCA in the EU. This robust funding environment enables modernization, expansion of capabilities, and strengthening of underlying payment mechanisms, positioning the sector for continued growth and innovation.

forces.title: Agentic AI Driving Demand for Advanced Payment Solutions
forces.description: The rise of agentic commerce and AI-native financial operating models is a significant upside driver for payment infrastructure. Agentic AI, capable of autonomous discovery, comparison, and execution of transactions on behalf of users and businesses, will demand specialized payment solutions. These solutions must support secure digital delegation, ensure traceable transactions, and integrate seamlessly with AI agents to optimize cash flow management, risk assessment, and cross-border trade. This shift will prompt increased investment in cybersecurity, digital identity management, and purpose-built payment infrastructure to enable seamless and intelligent automated commerce workflows.

forces.title: Expansion of UPI-Linked Cross-Border Payment Corridors
forces.description: The development and expansion of UPI-linked cross-border corridors represent a significant upside driver for India's payment infrastructure. These corridors are poised to enable faster, lower-cost, and more efficient cross-border remittances, payments, and trade settlements. By extending the reach and interoperability of UPI globally, India's payment mechanism can facilitate seamless international transactions, enhancing economic connectivity and supporting trade. This initiative leverages the success of domestic DPI to address pain points in cross-border payments, potentially expanding the functional scope and global relevance of India's payment systems.

viewpoints.title: India's DPI foundational for AI-led financial transformation and payment leverage
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views India's robust digital public infrastructure, especially UPI, as a distinctive foundation for AI-led transformation in the financial services sector. This infrastructure enables AI to support critical functions like underwriting, claims, servicing, and distribution decisions. By leveraging granular data from payment behaviors and digital journeys, UPI provides unique insights that allow insurers and other financial players to preassess risk, flag missing information, and personalize customer outreach at an unparalleled scale. This positions India's payment infrastructure at the core of advanced, data-driven financial innovation.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon

viewpoints.title: Interoperable B2B Layer to Transform Commerce with UPI Model
viewpoints.description: Bain and NPCI Bharat BillPay advocate for an interoperable digital layer, inspired by UPI, to revolutionize India's B2B commerce. This layer aims to connect business systems, ERPs, banks, and financiers, digitizing the entire order-to-cash cycle. By creating a secure, canonical information exchange rail, it can unify invoice, payment, and accounting records, resolving information asymmetry and enabling cash-flow based financing for MSMEs. This strategic infrastructure move promises enhanced transactional efficiency, improved credit access, and greater formalization across the business economy.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: India's DPI Poised to Lead Future Intelligent Financial Systems Globally
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts that India's digital public infrastructure, encompassing Aadhaar, UPI, and the Account Aggregator framework, has achieved unprecedented scale in democratizing financial access and fostering innovation. This success positions India uniquely to architect the next generation of intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial operating systems globally. The capability to build interoperable digital infrastructure that serves an entire population while remaining open for innovation is a key differentiator, enabling India to combine intelligence, trust, and scale for future-ready financial systems.

viewpoints.title: Fintech Nears Stablecoin Shift, Cautious on Regulation and Infrastructure
viewpoints.description: KPMG identifies that the global fintech market is at a pivotal point, poised for a "step change" driven by stablecoins and digital assets. This outlook acknowledges significant growth potential in these areas for payment infrastructure. However, the viewpoint is cautiously positive, highlighting persistent concerns among investors regarding the evolving regulatory landscape, the need for enhanced interoperability between systems and regions, infrastructure scalability challenges, and overall security. These factors are seen as crucial hurdles that must be addressed for the full potential of digital asset-based payment infrastructure to be realized.

viewpoints.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Paves Way for Programmable, AI-Native Payment Rails
viewpoints.description: Mastercard emphasizes that India's Digital Public Infrastructure, particularly its real-time payment rails, has profoundly expanded access to formal financial services. This foundation now mandates a shift towards financial infrastructure that is more programmable, AI-native, and inherently secure. The goal is to facilitate faster origination, smarter underwriting, more responsive servicing, and significantly more efficient domestic and cross-border payment flows. Mastercard believes this evolution, underpinned by network-level trust and robust governance, will enable the next generation of commerce through authenticated agents and tokenized, traceable transactions.

viewpoints.title: AI Transforming Digital Infrastructure into Intelligent Financial Ecosystem Layer
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights AI's emergence as the critical "intelligence layer" for India's fintech ecosystem, moving beyond simply supporting analytical decisions. Building upon the robust Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) foundation, AI is set to autonomously execute, optimize, and enhance fintech capabilities across financial services. This transformation will enable smarter real-time decisions, adaptive customer experiences, and more autonomous financial operations within the payment infrastructure. India's rich digital data ecosystems and supportive policy environment uniquely position it to scale responsible AI adoption and define the future of intelligent finance globally.

viewpoints.title: Payments as Platform for Scalable Growth, Infrastructure Investment Crucial
viewpoints.description: Courtney Trimble of KPMG International states that organizations increasingly perceive payments as a foundational platform for scalable growth and innovation. While modernizing and investing in new payment infrastructure is crucial, the significant opportunities lie in developing value-added services built *around* the payment rails. The focus is shifting beyond the payment mechanism itself to the tangible outcomes it delivers, such as optimizing cash flow, accelerating receivables, and streamlining payment workflows. This indicates a strategic evolution where robust infrastructure enables a broader ecosystem of financial services.

viewpoints.title: CBDC a Strong Foundation for India’s Future Digital Financial Infrastructure
viewpoints.description: Punjab National Bank's MD & CEO, Shri Ashok Chandra, views the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) as a robust foundation for the next phase of India's financial transformation. PNB's active participation in the CBDC ecosystem underscores its commitment to supporting this national digital infrastructure. This involvement aims to foster secure innovation at scale and aligns with the broader vision of creating an intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial operating system for India. The bank emphasizes the importance of balancing technological progress with strong governance and cybersecurity to preserve trust and resilience.

demand_drivers.description: Widespread smartphone access across India significantly contributes to the adoption and usage of digital payment methods, driving the overall index growth.
Foundational digital public infrastructure initiatives, such as UPI and Aadhaar, have provided the underlying rails and trust layer necessary for widespread digital payment adoption.

demand_drivers.description: UPI is used by roughly 500 million individuals, ensuring a high volume of transactions. The platform's accessibility and ease of use attract and retain a significant user base.
A vast network of 65 million merchants supports UPI transactions, driving demand for the payment system in everyday commerce and business-to-consumer interactions.

demand_drivers.description: UPI's widespread adoption as a digital public infrastructure drives massive transaction volumes, enabling financial inclusion and digital participation nationwide.

The ability to link nearly 2.9 billion financial accounts through the Account Aggregator framework facilitates secure data sharing, further enhancing the UPI ecosystem's utility and transaction activity.

market_sizing.methodology: Annual transaction volume processed by India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for the fiscal year.

demand_drivers.description: Large M&A deals, such as the Worldpay acquisition by Global Payments ($24.3 billion), significantly contribute to the overall investment figures, reflecting consolidation trends and a focus on market leadership.

Investors are prioritizing scaled, profitable, and infrastructure-focused businesses within payments, channeling larger amounts of capital into fewer transactions to drive efficiency and capability expansion.
